back: The sum of the random kinetic and potential energies of the molecules of a system; a function of its state.
$\Delta U = q + W$: $q$ = energy supplied by heating, $W$ = work done ON the system

front: Work done by a gas at constant pressure
back: $W_{\text{by}} = p\Delta V$ (area under the $p$-$V$ graph); $W_{\text{on}} = -p\Delta V$
No intermolecular forces → no potential energy → U is all random kinetic energy and depends only on T.
Melting or boiling: kinetic energy constant (constant T); potential energy, and so U, increases.
q = 0: compression → W > 0 → warms (bicycle pump); expansion → W < 0 → cools (aerosol).

front: Isothermal change of an ideal gas
back: ΔU = 0, so q = −W: energy supplied by heating equals work done by the gas.
Returns to the same state: ΔU = 0, so net heat in = net work done by the gas = enclosed area on p-V.
Some books use ΔQ = ΔU + W with W = work done BY the gas. Same law; state your convention.
